change: Apply the approved abstract with coarse and fine data combination motivated by generalization
previous_abstract:
Learning to predict physical fields such as temperature and velocity requires
fine simulation data that can be costly to obtain. Multifidelity learning
reduces this cost by combining inexpensive coarse solutions with a smaller
number of fine solutions. We present \method{}, an ensemble workflow
that automatically selects and combines nine field surrogate models.
For each dataset, ensemble fitting compares model predictions with known fine
solution fields at additional parameter inputs reserved from surrogate training.
These examples are used either to select the most accurate individual model
or to fit averaging weights by minimizing the combined prediction error.
Each model receives one weight across the entire field. The weights remain
fixed for new parameter inputs, which require no additional coarse solve.
We evaluate the workflow on 22 datasets spanning seven classes of partial
differential equations (PDEs) and climate emulation. Across the PDE datasets,
seven different models achieve the lowest error on at least one dataset.
We use five additional input and fine solution pairs
per dataset to fit ensemble weights and select the individual model with the
lowest error on those examples. The ensemble improves accuracy on 16 datasets.
Compared with the lowest error individual model, the ensemble reduces geometric
mean relative $L^2$ error by 11.6\% when averaged across PDE classes and 7.5\%
when averaged across all 22 datasets.
